Une planche de perles, et toute l'histoi: A board of beads, and the whole history of a kingdom.
Thomas Reefe publie dans la revue Africa: Thomas Reefe published in the journal African Arts an article presenting the lukasa as a Luba memory device.
The poet of the banquet dies at 90.
Selon le marbre de Paros, Simonide meurt: According to the Parian Marble, Simonides died in 468 or 467 BC, aged 90. Legend would make him the inventor of the art of memory.
Une école qui donnera son nom à toutes l: A school that would give its name to all academies.
Vers 383 av. J.-C., Platon fonde à Athèn: Around 383 BC, Plato founded the Academy in Athens, where teaching was done through dialogue.
La méthode des lieux passe à la télévisi: The method of loci goes on television.
La série Sherlock de la BBC montre son h: The BBC series Sherlock shows its hero storing his memories in "mind palaces": the method described two thousand years earlier.
Même les Anciens trouvaient certains pro: Even the Ancients found some prodigies suspicious.
Vers 95, dans son Institution oratoire,: Around 95, in his Institutio oratoria, Quintilian expressed surprise that anyone could have found 360 places in the twelve signs of the zodiac, as Metrodorus did.
Apprendre sans effort : la promesse magi: Learning without effort: the magical promise of the Middle Ages.
Au XIIIe siècle circule l'Ars notoria, l: In the 13th century, the Ars notoria circulated, a book of magic attributed to Solomon: prayers and figures were meant to give knowledge and memory. Students loved it.
Il voulait apprendre la mémoire. Il a li: He wanted to learn memory. He betrayed his master.
Le Vénitien Giovanni Mocenigo, qui voula: The Venetian Giovanni Mocenigo, who wanted to learn the art of memory, denounced Giordano Bruno to the Inquisition. Arrested on 22 May 1592, Bruno was burned in Rome in 1600.
Le palais de mémoire part en Chine: The memory palace goes to China
Un jésuite enseigne aux Chinois l'art de: A Jesuit teaches the Chinese the art of places.
Matteo Ricci écrit en chinois un traité: Matteo Ricci wrote in Chinese a treatise on mnemonics for the governor of Jiangxi: the European memory palace in the service of Chinese characters.
Aimé Paris publie la première version co: Aimé Paris published the first known version of the major system in its modern form: one consonant sound per digit, free vowels.
Sans répétition, un souvenir neuf s'évap: Without rehearsal, a new memory evaporates.
Le Britannique John Brown montre qu'en e: The Briton John Brown showed that when rehearsal is prevented, a few letters are forgotten in a few seconds. The Petersons confirmed it the following year.
Réviser juste avant d'oublier, de 5 seco: Review just before forgetting, from 5 seconds to 2 years.
Paul Pimsleur publie son rappel à interv: Paul Pimsleur published his graduated-interval recall: 5 seconds, then further and further apart, up to 25 days, 4 months and 2 years.
L'homme au monde en éclats: The man with a shattered world
Un soldat reconstruit sa mémoire mot à m: A soldier rebuilds his memory word by word.
Alexandre Louria raconte le combat de Le: Alexander Luria tells of the struggle of Lev Zasetsky, wounded in the brain during the Second World War, to recover his memory and his words.
Endel Tulving distingue la mémoire épiso: Endel Tulving distinguished episodic memory, that of lived experiences, from semantic memory, that of general knowledge.
Le chiffre magique tombe à quatre: The magic number drops to four
Nelson Cowan publie « The magical number: Nelson Cowan published "The magical number 4 in short-term memory": a young adult would hold about four chunks in mind.
Un chef d'orchestre, une boucle pour les: A conductor, a loop for sounds, a notepad for images.
Alan Baddeley et Graham Hitch proposent: Alan Baddeley and Graham Hitch proposed a three-part model of working memory: a central executive, a phonological loop and a visuospatial sketchpad.
Un indice ne marche que s'il était là au: A cue only works if it was there at the start.
Endel Tulving et Donald Thomson publient: Endel Tulving and Donald Thomson published the principle of encoding specificity: to help recall, a cue must overlap the memory trace.
Les premières études sur l'effet de test: The first studies on the testing effect
Edwina E. Abbott publie les premières ét: Edwina E. Abbott published the first documented experimental studies on the testing effect: trying to recall helps you remember.
Cinquante-quatre jeux de cartes, vus une: Fifty-four decks of cards, seen only once.
Le 1er mai 2002, Dominic O'Brien retient: On 1 May 2002, Dominic O'Brien memorised the order of 2,808 cards, 54 decks, looking at each card only once, with 8 errors.
Quarante jours pour une mémoire de champ: Forty days to a champion's memory
Martin Dresler et le champion Boris Konr: Martin Dresler and the champion Boris Konrad showed in Neuron that 40 days of training with places more than double the number of words remembered and bring the brain's connections closer to those of champions.
Hearing your name in the hubbub.
Colin Cherry nomme le problème de la soi: Colin Cherry named the cocktail party problem: we follow one voice among others, but catch our name in the one we are not listening to.
